reviewer: Claude coordinator and independent Claude review agents (text, illustrations)
text: Independent review agent read the full text against Ryder's The Dog Who Went Abroad and its frame (the monkey telling the crocodile); every Ryder beat is kept in order and every addition is disclosed.

No 'return to your own kind' moral: the ending weighs the dog's own greed against the city dogs' unkindness, and says peace is found among those who share, wherever they are. The verse about 'easy-going women' is replaced with disclosure.
Age band 8+: the bites are one calm sentence and the dog recovers; nobody dies.
Small fixes before approval (a missing speech verb, a lion's word for a dog). No em dashes; the pause question comes before the attack.
illustrations: Storyboard 1024x1536, under 650 KB; one Codex gpt-5.6-sol generation, no edits, seams exactly at x=512 and y=512/1024; no text.
Chukki keeps its tan coat, white chest, curled tail and brown left-eye patch; the black, grey and white city dogs stay the same trio.
The attack is shown only as a barking chase with no biting contact, blood or wounds; the famine is cracked land and leafless trees.
No people and no modern objects. One alt text was corrected after review to match the picture.
limitations: AI-agent editorial review, not human Kannada-teacher or scholar certification.
Age bands are editorial judgements against the README table and have not been tested with children, parents or adult readers.
Source fidelity was checked against saved copies of the Wikisource pages of Ryder's 1925 translation, not against Durgasimha's Kannada text or a Sanskrit recension.
Art was generated with Codex CLI on gpt-5.6-sol and judged on the full sheet and 512px panel crops with the grid measured in pixels; edited panels were re-checked by a separate agent.
